concept.title: Firefox 154 Media Stack Phase 2-3 Completion: WebCodecs Validation Gating & Unmodified File Cleanup
concept.human_rationale:
We completed Phase 2 and Phase 3 of the media stack audit by patching 6 files that control how websites request video decoding and encoding through browser APIs. The key insight: when a website tries to use VP8, VP9, or AV1 video formats through the WebCodecs API or WebRTC video calls, our patches now block those requests immediately at the validation stage, forcing the site to fall back to H.264 which our graphics chip handles efficiently. We also cleaned up 8 files that were copied for inspection but didn't need any changes, keeping the patch folder lean.
PROBLEM: After completing Phase 0 (core media pipeline gating) and Phase 1 (preference tuning), the browser still had unguarded entry points where websites could attempt to instantiate software video decoders and encoders through the WebCodecs JavaScript API, WebRTC peer connections, and the Media Capabilities API. These would bypass the core H.264 hardware-only policy and load VP8/VP9/AV1 software codecs onto the CPU, causing thermal throttling on the Ivy Bridge i7-3632QM.
